email.body1:
Frank, saw Nextech launched Cora Scribe and took Best in KLAS for ophthalmology EHR this year.

Momentum like that surfaces more specialty-practice accounts than the inside team can work before interest cools, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount, 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Nextech off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing those progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Frank, quick follow-up for Nextech.

With a new AI product and KLAS recognition driving demand, expectations on pipeline jump faster than inside-sales headcount can. Most teams don't know how many meetings they need to book to hit the number, so the gap surfaces late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Nextech needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Frank, last bit of proof for Nextech.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Nextech's reply rate likely compares to other specialty health-IT vendors. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Frank, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. A product launch is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to an inside-sales motion? I'll tailor it to Nextech either way.
